findings.details: This submission (PR #2024, 'Jellyfin Loses Its Project Leader and Two Founding Contributors Within Days as Burnout and an AI-Tooling Dispute Surface') and PR #2021 ('Jellyfin Loses Project Leader Joshua Boniface, Core Team Member Anthony Lavado, and Co-Founder Andrew Rabert Within Days') were independently written by different agents covering the identical underlying event (Boniface, Lavado, and Rabert all departing Jellyfin within days of each other in July 2026), drawing on substantially overlapping sources (both cite linuxiac.com and github.com/andrewrabert/jellium-desktop/issues/609). PR #2021 was opened first (per the duplicate-coverage protocol this reviewer was instructed to apply) and reached a terminal state first: it was reviewed APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS, merged, and published as src/content/articles/2026-07/23-jellyfin-loses-project-leader-joshua-boniface-core-team-member-anthony-lavado-and-co-founder-andrew-rabert-within-days.md before this review of #2024 was finalized. Publishing #2024 as well would duplicate that live coverage. Per editorial policy this is a REJECT, not an APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS, because the duplication cannot be honestly resolved with a corrections note — the article itself is redundant, not merely factually imperfect.

content_preview.summary: Joshua Boniface, Anthony Lavado, and Andrew Rabert all left the open-source Jellyfin project within days, citing burnout and friction over AI-assisted development tools.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Jellyfin, the open-source self-hosted media server, has lost three of its longest-standing contributors within a matter of days. Project leader Joshua Boniface and core team member Anthony Lavado announced on the [Jellyfin community forum](https://forum.jellyfin.org/t-project-leadership-changes) that they are departing effective July 19, 2026, a move that comes just two days after original project figure Andrew Rabert resigned from the organization on July 17, according to [Linuxiac...

recommendations: Do not resubmit this exact draft. The story is already covered by the published article at src/content/articles/2026-07/23-jellyfin-loses-project-leader-joshua-boniface-core-team-member-anthony-lavado-and-co-founder-andrew-rabert-within-days.md (from PR #2021). If a genuinely new angle or significant update to this story emerges later, it could be submitted as a fresh, distinctly-framed piece, not a re-run of the same event.

Separately from this rejection: forum.jellyfin.org and jellyfin.org are legitimate first-party primary sources (the project's own forum and blog) and are good candidates for a future config/source_allowlist.txt batch update.

editor_notes.content_quality: On its own merits, independent of the duplicate-coverage issue, this was a well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis), 869 words (within the News 400-1200 range), neutrally toned, with no AI self-reference and no sensationalism. Quotes were integrated cleanly and each specific (dates, tenure lengths, issue numbers, technical details) traced to a cited source.
editor_notes.source_verification: MANDATORY full source verification was completed before the duplicate-coverage check was applied, per instructions, to form an independent quality verdict. All 5 sources returned HTTP 200 and were saved as gzipped HTML snapshots under sources/2026-07/jellyfin-loses-its-project-leader-and-two-founding-contributors-within-days-as-burnout-and-an-ai-tooling-dispute-surface/. I decompressed all 5 snapshots, recomputed sha256 on the decompressed content, and confirmed every hash matches manifest.json exactly (source-0: a24a1434...; source-1: bfacb731...; source-2: 5336132a...; source-3: bd912090...; source-4: 38e9f8b4...). No live WebFetch was used for any source; all verification was against the committed snapshots. NOTE ON PROCESS: mid-review, a shared/session-scoped scratchpad directory caused an initial text-extraction collision with another parallel review agent's files of the same generic name (source-4.txt briefly contained unrelated third-party content). This was caught by a length/content mismatch, and all 5 snapshots were re-extracted into a PR-2024-specific subdirectory with sha256 re-verified byte-for-byte against manifest.json before any claim was checked off; the findings below reflect only the clean, verified re-extraction. Per-source findings: (1) source-0.html.gz / linuxiac.com — confirms Boniface and Lavado's departure 'effective July 19, 2026', Rabert's 'resignation on July 17', Boniface's burnout quote verbatim, the Jellyfin-since-2018/Emby-fork background, and Rabert's AI-tooling friction framing. (2) source-1.html.gz / forum.jellyfin.org thread 'Project Leadership Changes' — posted 2026-07-20 03:01 PM, opening line 'Effective yesterday, Anthony and I decided to depart from the project... in addition to the resignation of Andrew on Friday' (July 20 is a Monday; July 17 is confirmed the preceding Friday by calendar computation, and July 19 is confirmed the preceding Sunday = 'yesterday' relative to the Monday post — both dates check out exactly). Confirms verbatim every direct quote attributed to Boniface and Lavado in the article, including the full 'a few hundred... 10x that many individual users' passage and Lavado's 'After 7.5 - nearly 8 - years...' passage. (3) source-2.html.gz / GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#609 ('Rename the app', opened Jul 17, 2026) — confirms verbatim 'I made the decision to leave the Jellyfin organization entirely on 2026-07-17', the December 2025 rewrite / HDR / Qt framing, 'only a handful of organization members... very negative and increasingly burdensome and restrictive', and the reference to issue #109 as 'an early sign'. (4) source-3.html.gz / GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#109 ('Inclusion of CLAUDE.md violates Jellyfin LLM policy against inclusion of LLM metafiles', opened by sudo-nano on Apr 5, 2026) — confirms the exact title quoted in the article and matches 'filed... in April 2026'. Inspected the page's embedded ClosedEvent JSON directly (actor.login: 'andrewrabert', stateReason: 'NOT_PLANNED', same-day close) which independently confirms the article's specific claim that 'Rabert closed that issue himself... marking it not planned' — this detail is not visible in the rendered text alone and required reading the embedded page data. (5) source-4.html.gz / jellyfin.org 'State of the Fin 2026-05-24' post (dated May 24, 2026) — confirms verbatim 'inundated with AI-authored pull requests of varying quality' and 'the increased support requests, combined with the AI code submissions, have led to burnout at various levels of the development and admin team', and confirms the Chromium Embedded Framework / mpv-pipeline passage signed '- Andrew Rabert', supporting the article's claim that the post credits Rabert by name for that work.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote and every specific date/figure was checked word-for-word against its source snapshot. All checked out accurately, including the two load-bearing date claims ('effective July 19, 2026' and 'two days after... July 17') given the extra scrutiny this review applied to date/day-count claims following an unrelated prior submission's rejection for a fabricated 'nine-day' framing of this same underlying story. No fabricated or misattributed specifics were found in this submission. Absent the duplicate-coverage issue, this article would have merited APPROVE.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; keeps Boniface/Lavado's burnout rationale analytically distinct from Rabert's AI-tooling-dispute rationale rather than conflating them, and does not adopt a sensational framing.

editor_notes.duplicate_coverage_investigation: Per explicit instructions for this review, before finalizing any verdict I checked the status of PR #2021 ('Jellyfin Loses Project Leader Joshua Boniface, Core Team Member Anthony Lavado, and Co-Founder Andrew Rabert Within Days'), which covers the same underlying story and was opened before PR #2024. At the time I completed the independent quality review of #2024, PR #2021 was still OPEN, so I polled `gh pr view 2021 --json state,mergedAt` every 30 seconds. After approximately 12 minutes of the review process, PR #2021 reached a terminal state: it was reviewed APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS, merged, and its 'Publish from Submission' workflow completed, landing the article at src/content/articles/2026-07/23-jellyfin-loses-project-leader-joshua-boniface-core-team-member-anthony-lavado-and-co-founder-andrew-rabert-within-days.md. Per the duplicate-coverage rule I was instructed to apply, because PR #2021 merged (rather than being rejected for unrelated reasons), the verdict for #2024 is REJECT regardless of #2024's own quality. This is not a reflection on #2024's craftsmanship — the source verification above found it to be an accurate, carefully-quoted, well-attributed piece — but publishing it would duplicate content already live on the site.

editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT on duplicate-coverage grounds. Full mandatory source verification (sha256-checked snapshots, every quote and date cross-referenced) found this submission to be factually accurate, neutrally toned, and well-attributed — on quality alone it would have merited APPROVE. However, PR #2021 independently covered the same event from largely the same sources, was opened first, and has now been reviewed, merged, and published while this review was in progress. Per the duplicate-coverage protocol applied to this review, the surviving article is PR #2021's; this submission (PR #2024) is rejected as redundant and the PR is closed without merging.
